text:
Ivy: quick thought — what if we compress the usual deploy playbook into a single `/orchestra` macro? run pin -> preflight -> notes-gen -> notify. keep it optional to step through each stage.

Alex: interesting. like a non-interactive shortcut that still surfaces checks? :thinking_face:

Ivy: exactly. idea: `/orchestra start --profile=canary --pin=model:v2 --dry-run` then it outputs a compact checklist + links to logs and a generated release note draft.

Maria: i like the UX. big concern: migrations and DB locks. can the macro detect migration steps and pause for manual confirm?

Ivy: yeah — add a gating stage. proposed flags: `--pause-for-migrations` and `--sre-approval` so SRE can ack if needed.

Alex: also want a fast rollback hook: if any healthcheck fails during canary, we should auto-pin back to previous stable and post a rollback note. do we have that for the current deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: i can support that pattern. sample invocation:```/orchestra start --profile=canary --pin=web:2026-03-10 --dry-run=false --pause-for-migrations=true --sre-approval=true```returns: preflight summary, expected latency impact, migration checklist, and generated release notes draft.```

Ivy: here is a minimal release-note template i sketched (bot can populate):```Summary: Minor web service rollout (canary)
Why: perf fixes for token batching
Impact: brief increase in 95p latency during rollout, no schema changes
Rollback plan: pin web to 2026-03-08 on failure, alert #incidents
Rollout steps: 1) preflight, 2) apply pin, 3) confirm canary metrics
Contacts: @oncall-sre, @release-owner
```

Maria: can we also have a `--note-mode=compact|detailed` flag so product folks get a one-line and SRE get a full checklist?

Alex: +1. also request: annotate the commit hash and include a quick `curl` check snippet. example:```curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://staging.healthz | jq .status```

Ivy: good. one more thing — we should surface cost/slot impact for dedicated pools (so ppl know if they're using burst capacity). bot could query the quota API and add a single line to release notes.

srebot: SRE oncall gating: i can auto-assign the oncall when `--sre-approval=true`. will create an approval task and post a link. use `@srebot approve <thread_ts>` to ack.

Alex: how about dry-run output? needs to include simulated failures so we can test rollforward/rollback logic. maybe `--dry-run=fail-mode=healthcheck` to simulate a canary fail.

Ivy: agreed. let's keep the first pass lightweight: implement `/orchestra` as an alias that sequences existing deploy-bot commands and emits a single compact release note. later: UI to visualize steps in console.

Maria: action items: 1) Alex — prototype the sequence logic and failure simulation (due EOD Fri). 2) Ivy — write the compact note templates and add cost line. 3) deploy-bot — add flags: `--pause-for-migrations`, `--sre-approval`, `--note-mode`.

Alex: noted. i'll start a small repo `infra/orchestra` with a thin orchestrator script + tests. will ping here when draft PR is up. :rocket:

Ivy: thanks — this should cut typical deploy friction. tagging @release-team FYI. :eyes:
